reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs with no comment, which is what a compliant finding should look like — nothing is being raised against the counterparty.

The cited text supports the classification: Section 2.1(b) and 2.2(a) permit sublicensing to Ono's Affiliates without Array consent and expressly allow extension to Third Party manufacturers acting on Ono's behalf, satisfying the affiliate/contractor limb.

No at-will revocation exists: termination is limited to uncured material breach/insolvency under Article 13, and Section 13.1 converts the grants into fully paid-up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free licences on expiry — squarely within the preferred position.
Section 18.9 allows assignment without consent to an acquirer of substantially all business or assets, meeting the successor-transfer element (and exceeding the fallback).

Sub-preferred features (Array consent gate for Third Party Sublicensees/distributors, consent for intra-group assignment) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the playbook's instruction not to flag minor shortfalls; deterministic checks both pass and are consistent with the substance.
